'''David Williams''' [[Royal Society|FRS]] is a Welsh mathematician who works in [[probability theory]].

==Early life and education==
David Williams was born at [[Gorseinon]], near [[Swansea]], Wales. He was educated at [[Gowerton Comprehensive School|Gowerton Grammar School]], winning a mathematics scholarship to [[Jesus College, Oxford]], and went on to obtain a [[DPhil]] under the supervision of [[David George Kendall]] and [[Gerd Edzard Harry Reuter]], with a thesis titled ''Random time substitution in Markov chains''.<ref>[http://www.theses.com/idx/scripts/it3.asp?xml=Z:\index\idx\docs\all\13\it00392049.htm Index to Theses]</ref>

==Career==
Williams held posts at the [[Stanford University]] (1962–63), [[University of Durham]], [[University of Cambridge]] (1966–69), and at [[Swansea University]] (1969–85), where he was promoted to a [[personal chair]] in 1972.

In 1985, he was elected to the [[Professorship of Mathematical Statistics, University of Cambridge]], where he remained until 1992, serving as Director of the [[Statistical Laboratory, University of Cambridge|Statistical Laboratory]] between 1987 and 1991.<ref>{{cite web
  | last = Whittle
  | first = Peter
  | author-link = Peter Whittle (mathematician)
  | title = 1985–92 Martingales and the Mabinogion
  | work = A Realised Path: The Cambridge Statistical Laboratory up to 1993
  | publisher = University of Cambridge
  | orig-date = 1993
  | year = 2001
  | url = http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/History/2history.html#8
  | access-date = 24 January 2008
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131219080017/http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/History/2history.html#8
  | archive-date = 19 December 2013
  | url-status = dead
  }}</ref> Following this, he held the Chair of Mathematical Sciences jointly with the Mathematics and Statistics Groups at the [[University of Bath]].

In 1999, he returned to Swansea University, where he currently holds a Research Professorship.

Williams's research interests encompass [[Wiener process|Brownian motion]], [[Diffusion process|diffusion]]s, [[Markov process]]es, [[martingale (probability theory)|martingales]] and [[Wiener&ndash;Hopf]] theory.  Recognition for his work includes being elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1984, where he was cited for his achievements on the construction problem for Markov chains and on path decompositions for Brownian motion,<ref>{{cite web
  | title = Williams, David
  | work = Library and Archive catalogue
  | publisher = The Royal Society
  | url = http://royalsociety.org/DServe/dserve.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqSearch=RefNo=='EC/1984/38'&dsqDb=Catalog
  | access-date = 24 January 2008
  | archive-date = 12 March 2020
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200312080729/https://collections.royalsociety.org/dserve.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqSearch=RefNo%253D%253D%2527EC%252F1984%252F38%2527&dsqDb=Catalog
  | url-status = dead
  }}</ref> and being awarded the [[London Mathematical Society]]'s [[Pólya Prize (LMS)|Pólya Prize]] in 1994.<ref>{{cite web
  | title = LMS Prizewinners
  | publisher = London Mathematical Society
  | url = http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/pastwinners.html#polya
  | access-date = 24 January 2008
  | archive-date = 17 December 2005
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20051217180519/http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/pastwinners.html#polya
  | url-status = dead
  }}</ref>

One of his main discoveries is the decomposition of Brownian paths with respect to their maximum.<ref>
{{cite journal |last1=Williams |first1=David|date= 1970|title= Decomposing the Brownian path|url=https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183532112 |journal= Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume= 76|issue= 4|pages=871–873 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1970-12591-5|access-date=12 October 2020|doi-access=free}}
</ref>

He is the author of ''Probability With Martingales'' and ''Weighing the Odds'', and co-author (with [[Chris Rogers (mathematician)|L. C. G. Rogers]]) of both volumes of ''Diffusions, Markov Processes and Martingales''.

*''Weighing the Odds: a course in probability and statistics'', Cambridge University Press 2001
*ed. with J. C. R. Hunt, O. M. Phillips: ''Turbulence and stochastic processes. Kolmogorov´s ideas 50 years on'', London, Royal Society 1991
